subject: Termination for convenience scope, mid-term transfer obligations & notice window
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question about termination for convenience & transition obligations

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal at Acme has flagged two items in the draft MSA we wanted to surface before redlines go too deep: the termination for convenience (TFC) language is fairly broad and the auto-renew notice window is shorter than our procurement policy allows. Specifically: 

- They expect a 60–90 day notice window for auto-renew opt-out.
- They want explicit service-transfer obligations and a data handoff SLA if we terminate for convenience mid-term (the draft only references "reasonable assistance").

Can you share Redwood's standard compromise matrix for these items? If possible, attach the redline your side would be comfortable sending to speed legal review. Procurement is in the loop (procurement@acme.com).

Appreciate it — we want to keep timeline tight (goal: sign by end of June).

Best,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Acme Corp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about termination for convenience & transition obligations

Liam — thanks for the note and for surfacing Acme's policy.

Quick answers up front:
- We can accept a 60-day auto-renew opt-out notice for the pilot/initial term.
- For mid-term termination for convenience, we normally offer a short transition window (30 days) plus reasonable assistance; I understand Acme wants a firmer SLA and explicit handoff obligations.

I'm looping in our legal lead, Laura Bennett, to propose concrete redline language that balances risk and your operational needs. Karthik and I will review the commercial tradeoffs (termination fee / pro-rata credits) and come back with a single redline and a short rationale doc.

I've attached our initial draft redline to speed things up. If procurement needs a commercial summary, we can produce a 1-page table showing notice windows, fees, and service-transfer commitments.

Next steps:
1) Laura to propose redline + short justification (by EOD Thu).
2) Karthik to propose the commercial compromise (notice window vs termination fee).
3) Jordan to send combined package to Acme legal.

Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Attachment: Acme_MSA_Redline_20250611.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about termination for convenience & transition obligations

Adding the commercial perspective here. From a sales/ops POV the clearest compromise that preserves predictable economics is: 

- Auto-renew opt-out: 60 days (we accept).
- Termination for convenience: allow TFC but: 
  * 30-day transition assistance (no charge for assistance hours up to a cap), and
  * termination fee equal to 3 months of committed monthly recurring revenue (to cover provisioning and damping costs), OR pro-rated refund (customer choice) where applicable.
- Service transfer: we will provide a data export within 14 days of termination and reasonable handover for 30 days; any additional engineering migration work billed at our standard SOW rates.

If Acme absolutely requires a longer notice (90 days), we'd need to reduce the termination fee to 2 months MRR or commit to a phased offboarding plan.

Jordan — if Laura can propose legal language aligned to this, I think it will be acceptable to Acme procurement. Liam — please confirm whether the ability to choose between termination fee vs pro-rated refund is acceptable to you.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Jun 2025 16:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Question about termination for convenience & transition obligations

Thanks everyone — internal summary and proposed language below.

Summary of positions:
- Acme: prefers 60–90 day opt-out window; explicit transfer SLA and clearer obligations for mid-term TFC.
- Sales (Karthik): willing to accept 60 days; suggests 3 months MRR termination fee or pro-rated refund; 14-day data export + 30-day assistance window.
- Legal (Redwood): want to limit long tail liability, preserve ability to suspend services for nonpayment, and keep IP/usage protections.

Proposed redline (high level) — attachments include annotated MSA: MSA_Term_Summary_20250613.pdf
- Auto-renew: "Either party may elect not to renew by providing written notice at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current Term."
- Termination for Convenience: "Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice. If Customer elects termination for convenience during the Term, Customer may either (a) pay a termination fee equal to three (3) months of Customer's average monthly committed fees during the Term, or (b) receive a pro rata refund for prepaid fees covering the unused portion of the Term. Termination shall not relieve Customer of obligations to pay fees accrued prior to the effective date of termination."
- Transition and Data Export: "Upon termination, Redwood will provide a complete export of Customer data within fourteen (14) days and reasonable transition assistance for up to thirty (30) days at no additional charge. Any additional migration work requested by Customer will be performed under a separate statement of work and billed at Redwood's standard rates."
- SLA carveouts: "Redwood's service availability SLA shall not apply to periods of service suspension caused by Customer's breach or force majeure events; Redwood maintains the right to suspend services for payment disputes consistent with the Payment / Suspension section."

If Acme accepts the above, we'll produce a tracked redline and a one-page commercial summary (notice vs fee options) and circulate for signature. If Acme needs 90 days for opt-out, we recommend moving to a 2-month termination fee (instead of 3) and adding a phased transition schedule — happy to put options into the doc.

Liam — can procurement confirm whether Acme prefers the termination fee or pro-rated refund option? If you want, we can prepare two short alternatives for your legal/procurement to choose from.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: MSA_Term_Summary_20250613.pdf
